claims.text: Chemically or microstructurally distinct layers promote the formation of interfacial barriers, including residual-stress fields and nascent oxide films.
These interfacial barriers impede dislocation motion and time-dependent plastic deformation relative to homogeneous coatings.
The initial coating consists of alternating HEA layers with slight chemical or microstructural differences.
Such multilayer HEA protective coatings may be processed by mechanical alloying and spark-plasma sintering.
Elevated-temperature loading in the range of approximately 500–900 °C is suitable for assessing the proposed creep behavior.
The interfaces develop residual-stress fields during testing.
Protective interfacial oxides or stabilized phases may form during testing.
Mechanical-property mismatch between layers produces altered stress distributions at their interfaces under prolonged elevated-temperature loading.
Layer boundaries obstruct dislocation motion and slow recovery or other creep mechanisms.
Obstructing dislocation motion and recovery delays creep onset and reduces the rate of time-dependent plastic deformation.
Multilayer coatings will exhibit lower total creep strain than homogeneous HEA coatings.
Multilayer coatings will exhibit lower creep rates than homogeneous HEA coatings.
The presence of observable interfacial barriers will correlate with improved resistance to plastic deformation.
The interfacial mechanism is effective only within a limited temperature and stress range.
Extreme temperature or excessive oxidation can degrade or debond interfaces and diminish the multilayer benefit.
The respective contributions of residual stress and oxide formation have not been quantitatively separated.
The long-term evolution of the proposed interfacial mechanisms is not fully characterized.
Failure to observe a statistically significant reduction in creep strain and creep rate in the multilayer coating would falsify the hypothesis.
Absence of the proposed interfacial barriers, or lack of correlation between those barriers and creep behavior, would falsify the hypothesis.
